doc.title: Carmen Leggio interviewed by Monk Rowe, Tarrytown, New York, October 31, 1998

title: His father's later support and opera
summary: His father only heard him near the end, his mother was his supporter, and his father loved opera.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Did your father, you said he didn’t really say until he was on his death bed that you made the right decision, but did he ever come out and hear you play over the years?

Near the end. I did a couple of concerts at the library and so on, and he saw it. But my mother was really my greatest supporter, she was the one. But my father was mad at me all this time, until his death bed, which was amazing.
And he continued — you said he worked at General Motors?
Yeah. And then he had his own business, he had his own shoe repair shop and made shoes. In Italy they used to make shoes, not only fix them.
Did he ever get into jazz music himself?
No, no. Opera. His thing was opera.
